Verifier Strictness and Citation Faithfulness

Abstract

We study how the strictness of an automated verifier changes the measured rate of unsupported citations in agentic scientific synthesis. Verifiers disagree on which citations to flag.

1 Introduction

Agentic systems read papers and return cited answers. Whether a citation holds is usually checked by one fixed judge, and nobody audits that judge.

3 Method

3.1 Verifiers

We compare six verifiers at a matched catch rate of 0.90.9 on the gold set.

3.2 Results

On identical agent outputs the unsupported-citation rate ranged from 3 % to 18 % depending only on the verifier’s strictness.

Agreement.

Negative-specific agreement between verifiers was 0.27 to 0.30.

4 Limitations

Our gold set covers only English computer-science papers.
